sanskrit: tataḥ pakṣininādena vṛkṣabhaṅgasvanena ca babhūvus trāsasaṃbhrāntāḥ sarve laṅkānivāsinaḥ
english: Then, at the clamour of birds and the crashing of fallen trees, all the inhabitants of Laṅkā were seized with terror and confusion.

sanskrit: vidrutāś ca bhayatrastā vinedur mṛgapakṣuṇaḥ rakṣasāṃ ca nimittāni krūrāṇi pratipedire
english: Beasts and birds fled shrieking in fear, and terrible omens befell the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tato gatāyāṃ nidrāyāṃ rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ tad vanaṃ dadṛśur bhagnaṃ taṃ ca vīraṃ mahākapim
english: Then, when sleep had left them, the rākṣasī guards — their faces grotesque — beheld the grove in ruin and that great heroic monkey standing there.

sanskrit: sa tā dṛṣṭva mahābāhur mahāsattvo mahābalaḥ cakāra sumahad rūpaṃ rākṣasīnāṃ bhayāvaham
english: When the long-armed, mighty-spirited, immensely powerful one saw them, he assumed a form so tremendous as to strike fear into the rākṣasīs.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ girisaṃkāśam atikāyaṃ mahābalam rākṣasyo vānaraṃ dṛṣṭvā papracchur janakātmajām
english: Having seen that vānara — colossal as a mountain, immeasurably powerful — the rākṣasīs then questioned the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: ko 'yaṃ kasya kuto vāyaṃ kiṃnimittam ihāgataḥ kathaṃ tvayā sahānena saṃvādaḥ kṛta ity uta
english: "Who is this, whose is he, where does he come from, and for what purpose has he arrived here? And how did conversation come to pass between him and you?"

sanskrit: ācakṣva no viśālākṣi mā bhūt te subhage bhayam saṃvādam asitāpāṅge tvayā kiṃ kṛtavān ayam
english: "Tell us, wide-eyed one — have no fear, fortunate lady, dark-cornered eyes — what did this one do, conversing with you?"

sanskrit: athābravīt tadā sādhvī sītā sarvāṅgaśobhanā rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpāṇāṃ vijñāne mama kā gatiḥ
english: Then spoke the virtuous Sītā, beautiful in every limb: "What capacity have I to know rākṣasas who assume any form at will?"

sanskrit: yūyam evāsya jānīta yo 'yaṃ yad vā kariṣyati ahir eva aheḥ pādān vijānāti na saṃśayaḥ
english: "You yourselves know who he is and what he intends to do. A serpent alone truly knows a serpent's ways — there is no doubt of this."

sanskrit: aham apy asya bhītāsmi nainaṃ jānāmi ko 'nvayam vedmi rākṣasam evainaṃ kāmarūpiṇam āgatam
english: "I too am afraid of him; I do not know his lineage. I take him to be a rākṣasa who has come here having assumed any form he wished."

sanskrit: vaidehyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyo vidrutā drutam sthitāḥ kāś cid gatāḥ kāś cid rāvaṇāya niveditum
english: Having heard the words of the Vaidehi, some rākṣasīs remained hurriedly where they stood, while others went off swiftly to report to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya samīpe tu rākṣasyo vikṛtānanāḥ virūpaṃ vānaraṃ bhīmam ākhyātum upacakramuḥ
english: The rākṣasīs with their grotesque faces drew near to Rāvaṇa and began to describe the dreadful, mis-shapen monkey.

sanskrit: aśokavanikā madhye rājan bhīmavapuḥ kapiḥ sītayā kṛtasaṃvādas tiṣṭhaty amitavikramaḥ
english: "O king, within the Aśoka grove a monkey of terrifying form stands there, of boundless prowess, having held converse with Sītā."

sanskrit: na ca taṃ jānakī sītā hariṃ hariṇalocaṇā asmābhir bahudhā pṛṣṭā nivedayitum icchati
english: "And fawn-eyed Jānakī Sītā, though questioned by us repeatedly, is unwilling to reveal who that monkey is."

sanskrit: vāsavasya bhaved dūto dūto vaiśravaṇasya vā preṣito vāpi rāmeṇa sītānveṣaṇakāṅkṣayā
english: "He may be a messenger of Vāsava, or a messenger of Vaiśravaṇa, or one sent by Rāma with desire to search out Sītā."

sanskrit: tena tvadbhūtarūpeṇa yat tat tava manoharam nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ pramṛṣṭaṃ pramadāvanam
english: "By him, assuming a form suited to his power, your charming pleasure-grove thronged with various herds of animals has been entirely laid waste."

sanskrit: na tatra kaś cid uddeśo yas tena na vināśitaḥ yatra sā jānakī sītā sa tena na vināśitaḥ
english: "There is not a single spot he has not destroyed — save only that spot where Jānakī Sītā sits, that alone he left unharmed."

sanskrit: jānakīrakṣaṇārthaṃ vā śramād vā nopalabhyate atha vā kaḥ śramas tasya saiva tenābhirakṣitā
english: "Whether out of intent to protect Jānakī, or out of weariness — weariness is unimaginable in such a one — she alone was guarded by him."

sanskrit: cārupallavapatrāḍhyaṃ yaṃ sītā svayam āsthitā pravṛddhaḥ śiṃśapāvṛkṣaḥ sa ca tenābhirakṣitaḥ
english: "Even the tall Śiṃśapā tree, adorned with lovely shoots and leaves, beneath which Sītā herself had taken her seat — that too he left protected."

sanskrit: tasyograrūpasyograṃ tvaṃ daṇḍam ājñātum arhasi sītā saṃbhāṣitā yena tad vanaṃ ca vināśitam
english: "For this one of terrible aspect, you should ordain a terrible punishment: he it was who spoke with Sītā and who laid waste your grove."

sanskrit: manaḥparigṛhītāṃ tāṃ tava rakṣogaṇeśvara kaḥ sītām abhibhāṣeta yo na syāt tyaktajīvitaḥ
english: "O lord of the host of rākṣasas, who would dare address your Sītā — she who is held in your heart — unless he were one who has already abandoned regard for his life?"

sanskrit: rākṣasīnāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ hutāgir iva jajvāla kopasaṃvartitekṣaṇaḥ
english: Hearing the words of the rākṣasīs, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, blazed with fury like a sacrificial fire, his eyes whirling with wrath.

sanskrit: ātmanaḥ sadṛśāñ śūrān kiṃkarān nāma rākṣasān vyādideśa mahātejā nigrahārthaṃ hanūmataḥ
english: The mighty-splendoured one commanded a troop of rākṣasas called kiṃkaras — heroes fit to match himself — to seize Hanūmān.

sanskrit: teṣām aśītisāhasraṃ kiṃkarāṇāṃ tarasvinām niryayur bhavanāt tasmāt kūṭamudgarapāṇayaḥ
english: From that palace there issued forth eighty thousand of those swift kiṃkaras, iron maces and hammers in hand.

sanskrit: mahodarā mahādaṃṣṭrā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ yuddhābhimanasaḥ sarve hanūmadgrahaṇonmukhāḥ
english: Huge-bellied, with great fangs, terrible in form, immensely powerful, all were eager for battle, intent on capturing Hanūmān.

sanskrit: te kapiṃ taṃ samāsādya toraṇastham avasthitam abhipetur mahāvegāḥ pataṅgā iva pāvakam
english: They rushed upon that monkey where he stood at the gateway arch, charging with great speed like moths hurling themselves into a flame.

sanskrit: te gadābhir vicitrābhiḥ parighaiḥ kāñcanāṅgadaiḥ ājaghnur vānaraśreṣṭhaṃ śarair ādityasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: They struck the foremost of vānaras with ornate maces, with iron bars with golden armlets, and with arrows blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: hanūmān api tejasvī śrīmān parvatasaṃnibhaḥ kṣitāv āvidhya lāṅgūlaṃ nanāda ca mahāsvanam
english: The splendid, glorious Hanūmān, like a mountain in form, slapped his tail upon the ground and let out a great roar.

sanskrit: tasya saṃnādaśabdena te 'bhavan bhayaśaṅkitāḥ dadṛśuś ca hanūmantaṃ saṃdhyāmegham ivonnatam
english: At the sound of his roar they were seized with terror, and they beheld Hanūmān towering like a rain-cloud at the horizon.

sanskrit: svāmisaṃdeśaniḥśaṅkās tatas te rākṣasāḥ kapim citraiḥ praharaṇair bhīmair abhipetus tatas tataḥ
english: Yet undeterred by their master's command, those rākṣasas fell upon the monkey from every side with diverse and terrible weapons.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ sarvataḥ sa mahābalaḥ āsasādāyasaṃ bhīmaṃ parighaṃ toraṇāśritam
english: Surrounded on all sides by those warriors, the immensely powerful one seized a dreadful iron bar that lay propped against the gateway.

sanskrit: sa taṃ parigham ādāya jaghāna rajanīcarān
english: Taking up that iron bar, he struck down the night-roaming rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa pannagam ivādāya sphurantaṃ vinatāsutaḥ vicacārāmbare vīraḥ parigṛhya ca mārutiḥ
english: As Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, might seize a writhing serpent, so that hero, the son of the wind-god, grasping that bar, ranged through the air.

sanskrit: sa hatvā rākṣasān vīraḥ kiṃkarān mārutātmajaḥ yuddhākāṅkṣī punar vīras toraṇaṃ samupasthitaḥ
english: Having slain those rākṣasa kiṃkaras, the heroic son of the wind-god, still eager for battle, returned and stood again at the gateway.

sanskrit: tatas tasmād bhayān muktāḥ kati cit tatra rākṣasāḥ nihatān kiṃkarān sarvān rāvaṇāya nyavedayan
english: Then those few rākṣasas who had escaped from that terror reported to Rāvaṇa that all the kiṃkaras had been slain.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasānāṃ nihataṃ mahābalaṃ niśamya rājā parivṛttalocanaḥ samādideśāpratimaṃ parākrame prahastaputraṃ samare sudurjayam
english: On hearing that his mighty host of rākṣasas had been slain, the king's eyes rolled in fury, and he commanded Prahastas's son — unmatched in valour, most difficult to overcome in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kiṃkarān hatvā hanūmān dhyānam āsthitaḥ vanaṃ bhagnaṃ mayā caityaprāsādo na vināśitaḥ tasmāt prāsādam apy evam imaṃ vidhvaṃsayāmy aham
english: Then Hanūmān, having slain the kiṃkaras, fell into reflection: "The grove has been destroyed by me, but the shrine-palace has not been demolished. I shall therefore demolish this palace too."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya hanumān manasā darśayan balam caityaprāsādam āplutya meruśṛṅgam ivonnatam āruroha hariśreṣṭho hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: Having thus resolved, Hanūmān — displaying his power in his very bearing — leapt to the shrine-palace that rose lofty as the peak of Meru, and the foremost of monkeys, son of the wind-god, scaled it.

sanskrit: saṃpradhṛṣya ca durdharṣaś caityaprāsādam unnatam hanūmān prajvalaṃl lakṣmyā pāriyātropamo 'bhavat
english: And having subdued it, the irresistible Hanūmān, blazing with splendour atop the towering shrine-palace, resembled the Pāriyātra mountain.

sanskrit: sa bhūtvā tu mahākāyo hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ dhṛṣṭam āsphoṭayām āsa laṅkāṃ śabdena pūrayan
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the wind-god, assuming his vast body, boldly struck his arms together, filling Laṅkā with the sound.

sanskrit: tasyāsphoṭitaśabdena mahatā śrotraghātinā petur vihaṃgā gaganād uccaiś cedam aghoṣayat
english: By that great ear-shattering clap, birds were hurled from the sky, and from on high he proclaimed aloud:

sanskrit: jayaty atibalo rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ rājā jayati sugrīvo rāghaveṇābhipālitaḥ
english: "Victorious is the supremely powerful Rāma! Victorious is the greatly powerful Lakṣmaṇa! Victorious is King Sugrīva, protected by Rāghava!"

sanskrit: dāso 'haṃ kosalendrasya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ hanumāñ śatrusainyānāṃ nihantā mārutātmajaḥ
english: "I am Hanūmān, son of the wind-god, servant of Rāma lord of the Kosalas — he of unwearied deeds — the slayer of enemy armies!"

sanskrit: na rāvaṇasahasraṃ me yuddhe pratibalaṃ bhavet śilābhis tu praharataḥ pādapaiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: "A thousand Rāvaṇas would be no match for me in battle, as I strike with thousands of rocks and trees!"

sanskrit: ardayitvā purīṃ laṅkām abhivādya ca maithilīm samṛddhārtho gamiṣyāmi miṣatāṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: "Having ravaged the city of Laṅkā and paid homage to the Maithilī, my mission accomplished, I shall depart before the eyes of all the rākṣasas!"

sanskrit: evam uktvā vimānasthaś caityasthān haripuṃgavaḥ nanāda bhīmanirhrādo rakṣasāṃ janayan bhayam
english: Having thus spoken, that bull among monkeys, stationed atop the aerial palace on the shrine-terrace, let out a fearsome roar, spreading terror among the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā caityapālāḥ śataṃ yayuḥ gṛhītvā vividhān astrān prāsān khaḍgān paraśvadhān visṛjanto mahākṣayā mārutiṃ paryavārayan
english: At that great sound, a hundred shrine-guards advanced, bearing various missiles, javelins, swords, and battle-axes; hurling them in deadly volleys they surrounded the son of the wind-god.

sanskrit: āvarta iva gaṅgāyās toyasya vipulo mahān parikṣipya hariśreṣṭhaṃ sa babhau rakṣasāṃ gaṇaḥ
english: That host of rākṣasas, encircling the foremost of monkeys, appeared like the wide, mighty swirling eddy of the Gaṅgā's waters.

sanskrit: tato vātātmajaḥ kruddho bhīmarūpaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: Then the son of the wind-god, furious, assumed a terrible form.

sanskrit: prāsādasya mahāṃs tasya stambhaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam utpāṭayitvā vegena hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ tatas taṃ bhrāmayām āsa śatadhāraṃ mahābalaḥ
english: With great speed Hanūmān, the mighty son of the wind-god, wrenched out a great pillar of that palace, adorned with gold, and whirled it, that weapon of a hundred edges.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasaśataṃ hatvā vajreṇendra ivāsurān antarikṣasthitaḥ śrīmān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having slain a hundred rākṣasas as Indra slays demons with his thunderbolt, the glorious one, stationed in the sky, spoke these words:

sanskrit: mādṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi visṛṣṭāni mahātmanām balināṃ vānarendrāṇāṃ sugrīvavaśavartinām
english: "Thousands like me — mighty monkey-lords, powerful, all under Sugrīva's command — have been dispatched by the great-souled one."

sanskrit: śataiḥ śatasahasraiś ca koṭībhir ayutair api āgamiṣyati sugrīvaḥ sarveṣāṃ vo niṣūdanaḥ
english: "Sugrīva will come with hundreds, with hundreds of thousands, with crores, with tens of thousands — to exterminate every one of you!"

sanskrit: neyam asti purī laṅkā na yūyaṃ na ca rāvaṇaḥ yasmād ikṣvākunāthena baddhaṃ vairaṃ mahātmanā
english: "This city of Laṅkā will cease to exist, and you will be no more, and Rāvaṇa no more — because the great-souled lord of the Ikṣvāku line has sworn enmity against you!"

sanskrit: saṃdiṣṭo rākṣasendreṇa prahastasya suto balī jambumālī mahādaṃṣṭro nirjagāma dhanurdharaḥ
english: Commanded by the lord of rākṣasas, the powerful son of Prahastas — Jambumālī of the great fangs — marched out, bearing his bow.

sanskrit: raktamālyāmbaradharaḥ sragvī rucirakuṇḍalaḥ mahān vivṛttanayanaś caṇḍaḥ samaradurjayaḥ
english: He wore red garlands and red garments, was garlanded with flowers, wore bright earrings; large, with rolling eyes, fierce, unconquerable in battle.

sanskrit: dhanuḥ śakradhanuḥ prakhyaṃ mahad rucirasāyakam visphārayāṇo vegena vajrāśanisamasvanam
english: He twanged his great bow — rivalling Indra's own bow — with its beautiful arrows, speedily, with a sound equal to the thunderbolt and the lightning.

sanskrit: tasya visphāraghoṣeṇa dhanuṣo mahatā diśaḥ pradiśaś ca nabhaś caiva sahasā samapūryata
english: By the twanging report of that great bow, the cardinal directions, the intermediate quarters, and the sky itself were suddenly filled.

sanskrit: rathena kharayuktena tam āgatam udīkṣya saḥ hanūmān vegasaṃpanno jaharṣa ca nanāda ca
english: Beholding him approach in a chariot yoked to mules, the swift Hanūmān both rejoiced and roared.

sanskrit: taṃ toraṇaviṭaṅkasthaṃ hanūmantaṃ mahākapim jambumālī mahābāhur vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Jambumālī of the mighty arms pierced Hanūmān, that great monkey standing on the gateway arch, with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: ardhacandreṇa vadane śirasy ekena karṇinā bāhvor vivyādha nārācair daśabhis taṃ kapīśvaram
english: He struck the lord of monkeys with a crescent-headed shaft in the face, with a single barbed arrow on the head, and pierced his two arms with ten iron-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tasya tac chuśubhe tāmraṃ śareṇābhihataṃ mukham śaradīvāmbujaṃ phullaṃ viddhaṃ bhāskararaśminā
english: His copper-red face, struck by the arrow, shone beautifully — like a full-blown lotus in autumn pierced by the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: cukopa bāṇābhihato rākṣasasya mahākapiḥ tataḥ pārśve 'tivipulāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ śilām
english: The great monkey, struck by the rākṣasa's arrows, grew enraged; then he noticed nearby an enormous great boulder.

sanskrit: tarasā tāṃ samutpāṭya cikṣepa balavad balī tāṃ śarair daśabhiḥ kruddhas tāḍayām āsa rākṣasaḥ
english: The powerful one wrenched it up swiftly and hurled it mightily; but the furious rākṣasa shattered it with ten arrows.

sanskrit: vipannaṃ karma tad dṛṣṭvā hanūmāṃś caṇḍavikramaḥ sālaṃ vipulam utpāṭya bhrāmayām āsa vīryavān
english: Seeing that effort come to nothing, Hanūmān of fierce valour, mighty in energy, uprooted a vast śāla tree and whirled it.

sanskrit: bhrāmayantaṃ kapiṃ dṛṣṭvā sālavṛkṣaṃ mahābalam jambumālī mahābalaḥ cikṣepa subahūn bāṇāñ
english: Seeing the immensely powerful monkey whirling that śāla tree, the mighty Jambumālī let fly a great many arrows.

sanskrit: sālaṃ caturbhir ciccheda vānaraṃ pañcabhir bhuje urasy ekena bāṇena daśabhis tu stanāntare
english: He cut the śāla tree with four arrows, struck the monkey with five on each arm, with one arrow in the chest, and with ten in the broad expanse of his breast.

sanskrit: sa śaraiḥ pūritatanuḥ krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ tam eva parighaṃ gṛhya bhrāmayām āsa vegitaḥ
english: His body pierced full of arrows, seized by immense rage, Hanūmān snatched up that very iron bar and whirled it swiftly.

sanskrit: ativego 'tivegena bhrāmayitvā balotkaṭaḥ parighaṃ pātayām āsa jambumāler mahorasi
english: The exceedingly swift one, of overwhelming power, whirled and then drove that iron bar down upon the broad chest of Jambumālī.

sanskrit: tasya caiva śiro nāsti na bāhū na ca jānunī na dhanur na ratho nāśvās tatrādṛśyanta neṣavaḥ
english: Of him thereafter — no head remained, nor arms, nor knees; no bow, no chariot, no horses were to be seen there, nor his arrows.

sanskrit: sa hatas tarasā tena jambumālī mahārathaḥ papāta nihato bhūmau cūrṇitāṅgavibhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Thus swiftly slain by him, Jambumālī the great warrior fell dead to the ground, his ornaments and limbs crushed to powder.

sanskrit: jambumāliṃ ca nihataṃ kiṃkarāṃś ca mahābalān cukrodha rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Hearing that Jambumālī and the mighty kiṃkaras had been slain, Rāvaṇa blazed with fury, his eyes reddened with wrath.

sanskrit: sa roṣasaṃvartitatāmralocanaḥ prahastaputre nihate mahābale amātyaputrān ativīryavikramān samādideśāśu niśācareśvaraḥ
english: His eyes copper-red with swelling rage at the slaying of the mighty son of Prahastas, the lord of night-roaming rākṣasas swiftly commanded the sons of his ministers — men of exceeding valour and prowess.
